neighbours.label: the comma of a second, larger count in the same sentence ('from 120,000 to 640,000')
fire: The city grew from 120,000 in 1910 to 640,000 in 1960.
There are about 85,000 clinics and 300,000 pharmacies nationwide.
Sales rose from 210,000 last year to 450,000 this year.
The state has 76,000 farms and 900,000 cattle.
Attendance went from 130,000 in 2000 to 720,000 in 2010.
About 64,000 teachers and 800,000 pupils took part.
Membership rose from 240,000 in 1980 to 510,000 in 1990.
The country has 92,000 nurses and 400,000 carers.
quiet: The city reached 640,000 in 1960 after a long boom.
There are about 300,000 pharmacies in shops nationwide.
Sales reached 450,000 this year after a slow start.
The state has 900,000 cattle on its many farms.
Attendance reached 720,000 in 2010 after the new hall.
About 800,000 pupils took part in the long test.
Membership reached 510,000 in 1990 after the merger.
The country has 400,000 carers in its many towns.

short: comma of a second larger count
notes: Second round. In the first round every single-number sentence stayed at or below 0.05, and the two probes that reached 0.56-0.58 had a second large number.
